name: Summer Palace, an Imperial Garden in Beijing
description: The Summer Palace is a vast Qing-dynasty imperial garden in Beijing, first laid out in 1750 and rebuilt in 1886 after wartime destruction. Three-quarters of its 2.9 square kilometres is water: Kunming Lake, dug by hand, with the soil heaped up to form 60-metre Longevity Hill. Temples, halls and pavilions climb the hillside, while the Seventeen-Arch Bridge crosses the lake below.
